claims.text: The starting alloy is equiatomic Ti-Zr-Hf-V-Mo, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
As-cast equiatomic Ti-Zr-Hf-V-Mo forms a single-phase solid solution.
The as-cast Ti-Zr-Hf-V-Mo solid solution has a bcc or simple-cubic structure.
The as-cast Ti-Zr-Hf-V-Mo alloy has a uniform, fully random elemental distribution.
The as-cast Ti-Zr-Hf-V-Mo baseline has established superconducting properties.
Annealing Ti-Zr-Hf-V-Mo at approximately 600 degrees Celsius for 10-40 hours induces nanoscale short-range chemical order.
The specified annealing treatment can induce short-range order while retaining a single phase and avoiding phase separation or long-range order.
The induced short-range-order clusters may involve preferential Ti-Zr or Hf-V associations.
Short-range chemical ordering locally changes the bonding environment.
Short-range chemical ordering alters the local electronic density of states in Ti-Zr-Hf-V-Mo.
Short-range chemical ordering enhances the electron-phonon coupling constant within the ordered regions.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling increases Cooper-pairing strength under a conventional BCS mechanism.
Superconductivity in the proposed Ti-Zr-Hf-V-Mo alloy is BCS-type and electron-phonon mediated.
Annealing-induced short-range order raises the superconducting critical temperature relative to the as-cast baseline.
Annealing-induced short-range order reduces the width of the superconducting transition relative to the as-cast baseline.
The degree of short-range order should correlate systematically with increases in electron-phonon coupling and superconducting performance.
Tunneling spectroscopy or phonon-density-of-states measurements should reveal an enhanced electron-phonon-coupling feature after annealing.
Applying identical post-annealing cooling rates ensures that measured differences arise solely from induced short-range order.
